tasks.short: Research material structures and properties and document product-relevant findings.

steps.what: Define material-property research questions and characterisation methods
Conduct research measurements of material structures and properties
Record sample identity, conditions, results and measurement caveats
Calculate predefined property summaries and prepare research plots
Interpret material structure-property relationships and implications for products
Write the internal materials research findings and limitations

tasks.design: Configure characterisation record fields in a laboratory records system represented by {OPS_SYSTEM}, tested analysis in {DATA_PLATFORM} and a findings template in {DOCS}. The scientist chooses methods, conducts measurements, captures context and interprets the results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurement records, repeated plots and internal findings structure are prepared manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable sample identifiers and tested analysis routines can connect captured results to repeat summaries.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected material behaviour and measurement artefacts require scientific interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real structure-property relationship from experimental error.

ambition.what: Inspect another predefined property comparison on the same checked dataset.

tasks.altitude: Spend more research effort on mechanisms and product implications.

reach.learn: Preserve sample identity, units and test conditions.

evidence.claim: The digest describes an Irish ISO 17025 water laboratory replacing paper and spreadsheet processes through laboratory automation; this is an adjacent records example, not materials-research labour evidence.
Native records and tested summary routines could reduce repeated characterisation administration; the labour estimate is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The research includes measurement capture and internal findings. Task 20214 separately prepares audience-specific reports or manuals from completed findings; the internal record is not counted as that report.

The scientist produces sample identifier, method, conditions, result, unit, replicate and caveat in s3; all 12 retained hours include capture and checks. The s1 design supplies analysis definitions. Missing context or failed validation stops the affected analysis for manual investigation in s5.
Try native laboratory record fields and existing analysis tools first. Savings require repeated manual analysis preparation today, not existing automatic instrument calculations.
This property-characterisation study is distinct from the production-process feasibility experiment planned in task 9085 when both occur in the same project; shared actual work must be counted once.
unknowns: Existing instrument exports and current repeated plot preparation.
research_questions: Can the routine reproduce known characterisation summaries and preserve sample and unit provenance?

incremental.description: Maintain analysis routines and record structures against known datasets.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 repeated-characterisation scenario: B=100, R=75, gross=25; upkeep=5 gives central net=20. Scientific decisions retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine material modifications and document candidate development approaches.

steps.what: Retrieve evidence on material properties and previous development attempts
Define required material properties and application constraints
Develop ways to strengthen, combine or create materials
Compare candidate materials and determine promising development directions
Write material concepts, rationale and evidence gaps

tasks.design: Configure a linked development evidence view and material-concept template in {DOCS}. The scientist retains target definition, invention and candidate comparison; the template reduces repeated concept-record structure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prior attempts are hard to find and concept records repeat target and evidence details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and reusable concept fields can retain development context.
tasks.still_hard: Promising mechanisms do not establish manufacturability or real-world performance.
tasks.human_edge: Propose scientifically plausible approaches and recognise decisive evidence gaps.
tasks.altitude: Make development choices traceable without automating material invention.

reach.learn: Separate target performance, proposed mechanism and untested assumptions.

evidence.claim: Native development views and concept templates could reduce retrieval and repeated record structure; the proposed saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Material concept writing is included separately from invention and selection. Physical validation is not claimed completed by this determination task.

The scientist produces target properties, application constraints, candidate mechanism, supporting references and evidence gaps in s5; 15 retained hours include writing and checking. Unsupported mechanisms stay hypotheses.
Use native views and templates first. No model proposes or ranks new materials and no automated experiment or external send is implied.
There is no self-approval gate or saving for the concept record's same-system save.
unknowns: How much concept documentation repeats existing target and reference details.
research_questions: Does the concept template reduce clerical preparation while preserving uncertainties and rejected alternatives?

already_counted.description: Write and check the concept record.

incremental.description: Maintain development links and concept fields.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=92, gross=8; upkeep=2 gives central net=6. Invention and selection retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare source-based scientific reports, manuscripts, proposals and technical manuals.

steps.what: Select results and references for the requested scientific document
Specify arguments and structures for reports, manuscripts, proposals or technical manuals
Draft scientific prose from the selected evidence and outline

loop.purpose: Draft audience-specific scientific prose from a fixed evidence pack.
loop.input: Source passages, results, references, outline and intended claims.
loop.output: Draft text with source anchors and explicit unsupported sections.
loop.check: Scientist checks each number, reference and substantive statement against its source and intended meaning.
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported sections are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot assemble varied scientific explanations for different document purposes.

steps.what: Format the scientific document and place its referenced tables
Check and revise scientific claims, references and document completeness
Send the final document to the authorised external requestor

tasks.design: Start with native document templates in {DOCS}, use a bounded draft from selected results and references, and format the draft deterministically. The scientist checks the complete document and separately sends the exact final version through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience-specific prose and document layout are repeatedly prepared from completed results.
tasks.enabler_now: A fixed evidence pack can constrain prose drafting while native templates handle layout.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent explanation can overstate results or misrepresent a citation.
tasks.human_edge: Own the argument, scientific limitations and suitability for the requestor.

ambition.what: Prepare an additional checked document for a different scientific audience.

tasks.altitude: Spend more writing effort on meaning and evidence rather than first drafts and layout.

reach.learn: Define the document's intended use and required evidence.

evidence.claim: The digest reports fabricated references in generated literature reviews, supporting explicit source checks rather than invented citations.
Source-bounded drafting and native formatting could reduce document preparation; the labour estimate is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This scenario includes an external requestor and a real document send. Internal notebook findings in task 9087 are inputs, not duplicated audience-specific writing.

The scientist produces source passages, result and table identifiers, reference anchors and confidentiality constraints in s1, and claims and structure in s2. Their full time includes capture; missing evidence stops drafting for manual completion.
The s3 scientist produces the draft and table references consumed by s4. Missing or mismatched table references return to manual correction in s5.
Use native templates first. Internal author editing has no self-approval gate; s6 checks the exact final attachment and recipient.
unknowns: Document mix, existing templates and confidentiality restrictions on drafting tools.
research_questions: Does source-based drafting reduce total preparation after every claim and citation has been checked?

already_counted.description: Review and correct the source-based draft.

incremental.description: Maintain templates and source handling and test draft quality.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final document, attachment and authorised recipient; any edit or recipient change requires a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 document scenario: B=100, R=67.5, gross=32.5; upkeep=6 gives central net=26.5. Range allows substantial evidence checking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan laboratory experiments and write protocols to test materials-process feasibility.

steps.what: Retrieve previous feasibility results and laboratory method references
Define process feasibility hypotheses and measurable success criteria
Design laboratory experiments, controls and test conditions
Write the laboratory experiment protocol and required observations
Check whether the planned experiment can resolve the feasibility question

tasks.design: Configure a linked planning reference view and experiment-protocol template in {DOCS}. The scientist defines hypotheses and controls, writes the protocol and checks that it can answer the feasibility question.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding prior methods and repeating protocol structure takes time around experimental design.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference links and reusable method sections can simplify protocol preparation.
tasks.still_hard: A well-written protocol may still fail to distinguish competing explanations.
tasks.human_edge: Choose controls, conditions and success criteria that establish meaningful feasibility.
tasks.altitude: Make experimental intent and limitations explicit in the written plan.

reach.learn: Identify required conditions, observations and unresolved design questions.

evidence.claim: Native planning views and protocol templates could reduce retrieval and repeated writing; the proposed experiment-planning saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Protocol writing is inside the planning task and separately priced from scientific design. This task does not execute the experiment.

The scientist produces hypotheses and criteria in s2, conditions and controls in s3, and sequence, observations and method references in s4. Its 17.5 retained hours include protocol capture; unresolved conditions remain explicit for manual design revision.
Use native references and templates first. No AI chooses experimental conditions or starts equipment.
The final plan check is scientific revision, not an invented author approval requirement. No separate save-time saving is claimed.
unknowns: How much protocol writing is repeated method structure.
research_questions: Can a native protocol template reduce writing while preserving all experiment-specific controls and limitations?

already_counted.description: Write and check the experiment protocol.

incremental.description: Maintain method links and protocol structure.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=89.5, gross=10.5; upkeep=2 gives central net=8.5. Experimental judgement retains all its time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep materials invention and experimental judgement human while reducing repeated calculations and document preparation.
reach: Connect samples, evidence, experiment plans and scientific documents.
role.ambitious_version: A materials scientist who can trace every proposed application and scientific claim to its evidence and limitations.
